item.title: [Boston Sports Journal] Red Sox sweep doubleheader as Wilyer Abreu delivers late; Gasper likely out for Yankees
item.dc:creator: Chris Henrique
item.description: By the time the Red Sox took the field for the second game of Friday’s doubleheader, their postseason destination was already set. They still found a way to finish a long day at Fenway Park with another win. Wilyer Abreu snapped an 0-for-11 skid with a two-run double in the eighth inning, while Brayan Bello and Jedixson Paez combined for a shutout as the Red Sox completed a doubleheader sweep of the Cubs with a 2-0 victory. item.content:encoded:
By the time the Red Sox took the field for the second game of Friday’s doubleheader, their postseason destination was already set.
They still found a way to finish a long day at Fenway Park with another win.
Wilyer Abreu snapped an 0-for-11 skid with a two-run double in the eighth inning, while Brayan Bello and Jedixson Paez combined for a shutout as the Red Sox completed a doubleheader sweep of the Cubs with a 2-0 victory.
Boston improved to 87-74 after winning the opener, 4-3, earlier Friday. That victory locked the Red Sox into the No. 5 seed in the American League and officially set up a rematch with the Yankees in the best-of-three Wild Card Series beginning Tuesday at Yankee Stadium.
With the standings no longer a concern, the rest of the weekend is about getting ready for New York.
Abreu entered Game 2 mired in a difficult September, carrying a .622 OPS for the month. He had gone hitless in his first seven at-bats of the doubleheader, including two strikeouts, before stepping to the plate with two outs in the eighth.
This time, Abreu delivered, ripping a two-run double to break a scoreless tie and give Boston a 2-0 lead.
The hit snapped an 0-for-11 skid for Abreu, whose streaky nature has been on display over the past two months. He posted a .971 OPS in August before cooling considerably in September.
After reaching base four times and collecting three extra-base hits in Game 1, Roman Anthony went 1-for-3 with a walk in the nightcap. He finished the doubleheader 4-for-6 with two doubles, a triple and two walks. Over his last six games, Anthony is 10-for-28 (.357) with six extra-base hits.
For an offense that has struggled throughout September, getting its leadoff hitter hot heading into the postseason could provide a significant boost.
The pitching was the bigger story in Game 2, with Bello continuing his impressive turnaround by tossing four scoreless innings against the Cubs.
His season looked much different before a demotion to Triple-A Worcester. Since returning to the majors, Bello has allowed one run or fewer in 12 of his 14 appearances, posting a 2.11 ERA with 13 runs allowed over 55 1/3 innings.
Bello isn’t expected to start during the Wild Card Series, but his work since returning from Worcester has strengthened his case for a spot on the postseason roster, where he could return to his role out of the bullpen.
Paez provided length to the bullpen in Game 2, allowing Chad Tracy to rest his relievers with the travel day coming on Saturday.
The Red Sox recalled the 22-year-old between games after optioning Raymond Burgos, who earned the save with two scoreless innings in the opener.
Paez’s first appearance with Boston on Sept. 1 was one to forget. He surrendered eight runs over 3 2/3 innings against Seattle. Paez replaced Bello and tossed five scoreless innings to finish the game, limiting the Cubs to three hits without issuing a walk while striking out four.
Paez became the first Red Sox pitcher to finish a victory with at least five scoreless innings since Scott Taylor threw 6 2/3 scoreless innings against the Yankees on Oct. 3, 1992. The right-hander is also just the fifth pitcher in franchise history to accomplish the feat within his first five career games and only the second in the last 70 years, joining Taylor.
The Red Sox finished their 2026 slate at Fenway Park with a 41-39 record after sweeping Friday’s doubleheader. Boston also secured its first series victory since Sept. 15, finishing the season 24-26-2 in series play and 11-14-1 at home. The Red Sox won 18 of their final 30 series overall, including 10 of their final 16 at home dating to June 12.
With a nor’easter expected to impact New England this weekend, Major League Baseball moved Sunday’s finale to Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg. The Red Sox and Cubs will fly to Florida following Friday’s doubleheader and play Sunday at 3:05 p.m.
Gasper Likely Out for Wild Card Series
Mickey Gasper will likely miss the Red Sox’ Wild Card Series against the Yankees after suffering a right biceps injury during Friday’s 4-3 win over the Cubs, according to MassLive’s Chris Smith.
The Red Sox officially termed the injury “right biceps discomfort.”
Gasper started behind the plate and appeared to injure his biceps while swinging through a pitch for a strikeout in the fifth inning. He was removed immediately, with Connor Wong replacing him at catcher to begin the sixth.
“I think he’s going over to get an MRI right now,” Tracy said after the game. “He’s in some pretty good discomfort. So I don’t know exactly what it is but he struck out on that last swing and had some discomfort in his biceps.”
Following the Game 2 win, Tracy told reporters that Gasper suffered a significant biceps injury.
Chad Tracy confirms after the game that it looks like a "significant" biceps injury for Mickey Gasper.
"It's probably going to take him out."
Brutal. pic.twitter.com/ncoEQrgFhr
The timing is particularly unfortunate for Gasper, who had carved out a meaningful role in Boston’s lineup. The 30-year-old is batting .251 with 10 doubles, nine home runs and 24 RBI while making starts at catcher, first base and designated hitter.
Between Boston and Triple-A Worcester, Gasper has hit 19 home runs this season. His likely absence also creates another decision as the Red Sox construct their Wild Card roster.

item.content:encoded:
Wilyer Abreu has been one of Boston’s most impactful all-around players, but lately the talented right fielder has been stuck in a serious rut.
Over the past few weeks Abreu has seen his offensive production fall off a cliff. Coming into the day he was batting .177 with a .546 OPS and four extra-base hits over his last 17 games since Sept. 3, and during Friday’s doubleheader he started 0 for 7 his first seven trips to the plate.
That kind of slump will put a strain on anyone’s confidence, but after striking out in the bottom of the sixth, Abreu said he was approached by veteran teammate Sonny Gray, who gave him a badly needed pep talk.
“It helped me a lot,” Abreu said. “He’s a vet, he’s got a lot of years here and how to handle those situations, so he give me good advice to feel good with my body, with my athleticism, and trust myself, try to get my confidence back and that was huge.”
The next time up, Abreu reminded everyone at Fenway Park who he really is.
Abreu’s go-ahead two-run double in the bottom of the eighth was the difference in Friday night’s 2-0 win over the Chicago Cubs. The right fielder stepped to the plate with two on and two outs in a scoreless game and crushed an opposite-field line drive high off the Green Monster.
That swing helped the Red Sox seal the doubleheader sweep, and the two clubs will now fly to St. Petersburg to get out ahead of the impending nor’easter to finish the regular season on Sunday at Tropicana Field.
In what was likely his final appearance of the regular season, Brayan Bello capped off his season of turbulence and redemption in style. The right-hander threw four-plus scoreless innings, held the Cubs to four hits and a walk and struck out two while throwing 39 of his 58 pitches for strikes.
Bello wraps up the year with a 4.33 ERA, a deceptively average mark for what was an extraordinarily unique journey. After earning himself a demotion following a disastrous first half that saw him lose his spot in the rotation, Bello finished the season with a 2.11 ERA over 55 1/3 innings in his last 14 appearances since being called back up just prior to the All-Star break.
Following the game Bello said he’s happy and grateful for the way his season ended, adding that the whole year was a big learning experience.
“I learned not to let bad moments dictate how the next one is going to be,” Bello said via interpreter Carlos Villoria Benítez. “Also I learned how to compete in the zone, I feel like in the second half I was able to compete in the zone and beat hitters in the zone, something that I wasn’t able to do in the first half.”
Bello gave way to rookie Jedixson Paez, who was called up between the two games and who has also endured an eventful first year in the majors. The 22-year-old had never pitched above Single-A prior to this season before he was poached by the Chicago White Sox in the Rule 5 Draft, and the right-hander made three uninspiring appearances for the White Sox before he was returned to Boston.
After spending most of the season in the Red Sox minor league system, he was called back up for a spot start on Sept. 1 and got shelled, allowing eight runs in 3 2/3 innings in a loss to the Seattle Mariners. But needing to cover some innings ahead of the club’s upcoming playoff run, Paez came through and gave the Red Sox five scoreless frames in what was by far the best outing of his MLB career so far.
“The first chance he got it didn’t probably go how he wanted and he gets another opportunity and goes out there and spins five scoreless innings and attacks the zone,” said Red Sox manager Chad Tracy. “It was awesome.”
Offensively the Red Sox were stymied by Cubs starter David Peterson, who held Boston to three hits and two walks over five shutout innings. The Red Sox had runners reach third base in both the third and fourth innings but couldn’t get the go-ahead runner home.
Boston didn’t fare much better against the Cubs bullpen, but the Red Sox finally got another chance in the bottom of the eighth when Isiah Kiner-Falefa and Jahmai Jones each walked to put two men on with two outs.
That brought Abreu to the plate to face left-hander Ryan Rolison, and the outfielder smoked an opposite-field line drive 100.5 mph off the bat high off the Green Monster. Kiner-Falefa and Jones both came around to score, and that was all she wrote.
Paez returned for the top of the ninth despite initially seeming to deal with a cramping issue while warming up, but after a brief visit by the trainer, he stayed in the game and sent the Cubs down 1-2-3 to end the game.
With this weekend’s finale relocated to St. Petersburg, Fla., Friday night marked the final regular season game at Fenway Park this season. The next time the Red Sox are back in Boston, it will either be for Game 3 of the American League Divisional Series against the Tampa Bay Rays, or for the end-of-the-season press conference should the club lose to the Yankees in the Wild Card round again.
Before they even knew when and where their last game would be, Tracy told his players to prepare to spend 11 days on the road, and Abreu said the team is determined to bring playoff baseball back to Fenway Park for the first time since 2021.
“I think the fans deserve it,” Abreu said. “It’s been five years that Boston hasn’t seen any playoff games, so I think we have to give them that opportunity to see playoff games again here at Fenway Park.”
In the meantime, the Red Sox and Cubs will play one more at Tropicana Field on Sunday starting at 3:05 p.m.

item.content:encoded:
Wilyer Abreu broke a scoreless deadlock with a two-out, two-run double in the eighth inning, lifting the Boston Red Sox to a 2-0 win and a doubleheader sweep over the visiting Chicago Cubs on Friday evening.
Abreu was in a 0-for-11 slump before smacking the big hit high off the Green Monster in left-center field. Isiah Kiner-Falefa and Jahmai Jones both walked to set the stage for Abreu’s heroics, with the first walk coming off Chicago’s initial reliever Javier Assad (6-2) in an eventual loss.
The Red Sox (87-74) were limited to just four hits, but Jedixson Paez (1-1) made them stand up while dealing the final five innings en route to his first big-league win. Paez, who was recalled from Triple-A Worcester in between games, scattered three hits, struck out five and did not issue a walk in relief of starter Brayan Bello.
The Cubs (88-73) had seven hits, including two apiece by Seiya Suzuki, Michael Busch and Nico Hoerner.
After Chicago starter David Peterson fanned six across five innings of three-hit ball, Assad had struck out the heart of the Boston lineup in order in the sixth and retired the first six men he faced.
Bello escaped a near-immediate jam in the first. After striking out leadoff hitter Pete Crow-Armstrong, Suzuki walked and Busch dunked a single into shallow left field, but back-to-back outs in the air ended the threat.
The Boston righty also induced double plays to halt potential rallies after leadoff singles by Hoerner in the second and Busch in the fourth. Kiner-Falefa made a diving stop and spun a 4-6-3 ball to erase Hoerner.
Paez replaced Bello following Hoerner’s leadoff knock in the fifth. Matt Shaw lined a two-out single that ricocheted off the umpire standing up the middle before runners were stranded on the corners.
Meanwhile, the Red Sox were hitless until Kiner-Falefa opened the third with a line-drive single to center. He reached third on Anthony’s knock to right, but Peterson retired the next two.
In the fifth, a leadoff walk to Kiner-Falefa was wasted.
The teams’ season finale was moved to Sunday at a neutral location in St. Petersburg, Fla., due to inclement weather expected to impact Boston all weekend.
–Field Level Media

item.content:encoded:
Los Medias Rojas de Boston pasaron la escoba a los Cachorros de Chicago, en la doble cartelera que se llevó a cabo este viernes en Fenway Park. A primera hora los Patirrojos triunfaron con pizarra de 4×3, y luego pintaron de blanco a los Oseznos, dos carreras por cero. Desafío donde lució el criollo Jedixson Páez en su retorno al Big Show.
Lee también: Justin Verlander se despedirá este sábado
Páez (1-1), ingresó al montículo en la parte baja del quinto episodio, en relevo del dominicano Brayan Bello. Completando una actuación realmente descollante.
El de Tinaquillo, se mantuvo en la lomita hasta el final del choque, dejando 5.0 entradas en las que aceptó tres imparables y recetó a cinco toleteros de Chicago. Salida que le permitió nivelar su récord en un triunfo por una caída y reducir considerablemente su efectividad de 18.90 a 10.80 luego de cinco presentaciones en el año.
La derrota fue a la cuenta del mexicano, Javier Assad (6-2), a quien en 2.1 innings lanzados le pisaron el plato en una ocasión
El también venezolano, Wilyer Abreu, fue el principal baluarte de la ofensiva del conjunto dirigido por Chad Tracy, al conectar de 4-1, con su doble 38 de la campaña y par de impulsadas, arribando a 76.
El pasar la escoba a los Cachorros mejoró el registro del conjunto de Massachussets a 87-74. Tercer lugar en la División Este de la Liga Americana.

item.content:encoded:
BOSTON (AP) — Wilyer Abreu hit a two-run double in the eighth inning, and the Boston Red Sox beat the Chicago White Sox 2-0 Friday night to sweep a doubleheader.
Brayan Bello allowed four hits over four innings and rookie Jedixson Páez (1-1) gave up three hits in five innings with four strikeouts in his first big league win.
Other WRAL Top Stories
Chicago dropped two games back of San Diego for the top NL wild card. The Padres hosted Arizona later Friday.
Javier Assad (6-2) was the loser. Chicago starter David Petersen allowed three hits over five innings and struck out six.
In the first game, Connor Wong hit a tiebreaking double in the seventh inning, to help the Red Sox rally from a three-run deficit in a 4-3 win that clinched the No. 5 seed in the AL playoffs.
Boston will play its Wild Card Series for the second year in a row at the New York Yankees, who won last season’s best-of-three matchup 2-1. It will be the seventh Red Sox-Yankees postseason series.
Friday’s opener was originally scheduled for Sunday afternoon but was moved up because a significant storm was forecast. The series finale, which had been slated for Saturday night, will now be played on Sunday afternoon in St. Petersburg, Florida.
Up Next
Neither team had announced Sunday pitching plans.

item.content:encoded:
The Red Sox are bringing in a fresh arm for the second game of Friday’s doubleheader.
After pitching on back-to-back days and throwing a combined 61 pitches, left-hander Raymond Burgos is being optioned to clear space for rookie right-hander Jedixson Paez.
Burgos threw the final two innings of Boston’s last two games, tossing two scoreless innings in Thursday’s 1-0 loss to the Cleveland Guardians before earning the save with two scoreless innings in Game 1 of Friday’s doubleheader against the Chicago Cubs.
Having taken on that level of workload Burgos likely wouldn’t have been available to pitch again until Sunday at the earliest, and he certainly wouldn’t have been an option out of the bullpen in Friday’s Game 2.
Paez has had a rocky rookie season in the majors. The 22-year-old was plucked from the Red Sox system by the Chicago White Sox in last winter’s Rule 5 Draft and made his MLB debut this past March. Paez made three appearances with the White Sox before being returned back to Boston, where he remained in the minors for the majority of the season until he was called back up for the club’s Sept. 1 game against the Seattle Mariners.
Paez allowed eight runs on 10 hits and two walks over 3 2/3 innings in that game, and through his first four big league appearances he has posted an 18.90 ERA over 6 2/3 career innings.

item.content:encoded:
BOSTON, MA—The Boston Red Sox today recalled right-handed pitcher Jedixson Paez. To make room, Boston optioned left-handed pitcher Raymond Burgos following the first game of today’s doubleheader against the Chicago Cubs.
Paez, 22, has pitched in four Major League games (one start) this season with the Chicago White Sox (three games) and Red Sox (one start), his Major League debut, allowing 14 runs with three strikeouts over 6.2 innings. The right-hander has also posted a 3.69 ERA (29 ER/70.2 IP) with 82 strikeouts in 22 games (12 starts) between Double-A Portland (17 games, seven starts) and Triple-A Worcester (five starts) this season. Signed by Boston as an international free agent in January 2021, the Venezuela native owns a 3.31 ERA (139 ER/378.1 IP) with a 1.05 WHIP and 389 strikeouts in 95 career minor league games (70 starts).
Burgos, 27, earned his second save of the season in the first game of today’s doubleheader against the Cubs, tossing 2.0 scoreless innings. The left-hander owns a 4.22 ERA (10 ER/21.1 IP) in nine appearances for Boston this season. He has also pitched in 17 games (15 starts) for Worcester, recording a 5.14 ERA (40 ER/70.0 IP) with 58 strikeouts. Originally selected by Cleveland in the 18th round of the 2016 First-Year Player Draft, the Puerto Rico native owns a 4.43 ERA (11 ER/22.1 IP) in 10 career Major League games with the San Francisco Giants (2024) and Red Sox (2026).

item.content:encoded:
Garrett Crochet reached an important milestone in his road to recovery on Tuesday, facing live hitters on the mound at Fenway Park for the first time since his ill-fated comeback attempt in late May.
Throwing live batting practice against Ceddanne Rafaela, the Red Sox ace threw 16 pitches, one more than originally planned because he spiked a changeup into the dirt on what was supposed to be his final pitch. The left-hander said he was able to ramp up his intensity to a level he hadn’t reached yet, that his fastball was in the 94-96 mph range, and that following the session he got good feedback from Rafaela.
With that crucial box checked, could Crochet’s next time on the mound come in a game setting? Crochet said it’s too soon to say, but he’s cautiously optimistic about his ability to do so.
“You don’t know until you know I suppose. I would say the way that live just went that I could go get outs,” Crochet said. “It depends, obviously, what role they want me in, like I said it’s not really for me to say, I know myself and I know my body, and the biggest thing is that I felt good out there.”
Crochet has missed the majority of the season due to left shoulder inflammation, which landed him on the injured list in late April after only six starts. What was originally believed to be a short-term injury wound up sidelining Crochet for five months and counting, but after Tuesday’s session there remains a possibility Crochet could factor into the postseason equation for the Red Sox out of the bullpen.
That will be up to chief baseball officer Craig Breslow and manager Chad Tracy, Crochet was sure to emphasize.
“This team has had a great year, I think for me to take a spot on the roster then someone would have to lose one, and I would feel bad doing that because this team has pitched their (butts) off the whole season,” Crochet said. “Ultimately that’s going to be something that’s up to the front office and whenever they gauge that I’m ready then I’ll accept that, and in the meantime I’m just going to keep working my butt off.”
Tracy said he was encouraged by Crochet’s outing, noting that his velocity is climbing and the spin on his pitches looked sharp. The next step will be seeing how his body recovers in the upcoming days and mapping out a plan for the weekend.
“What that looks like now, I don’t know,” Tracy said. “I just know that whatever it is it’s going to be done with Garrett’s best interest in mind.”
Typically the next stage in a throwing progression after throwing live batting practice would be to start a rehab assignment, but given that the minor league season ended this past weekend, that isn’t an option for Crochet. Time also isn’t on the left-hander’s side, so if Crochet is going to pitch in a game before the playoffs, he would have to be activated at some point over the final homestand.
Tracy said those are all factors the club is considering, and while he believes Crochet would be up for the challenge of jumping right into a playoff series, they have to be realistic about where he’s at when it comes time to decide who will be on the playoff roster.
“Knowing the player, if he was healthy and we felt he could he’d probably be like ‘I’m not going to be afraid of that,'” Tracy said. “That being said, we have to consider it and just be very mindful of what are we potentially exposing him to and what can he give us, really? Understanding you don’t want to leave yourself short, so for me it’s been step by step, the next step would be sometime this weekend, let’s see what that entails, and we’ll go from there.”
Rafaela, Contreras getting close
Ceddanne Rafaela (right quad strain) and Willson Contreras (bruised right hand) remain sidelined with their respective injuries, but Tracy said both are getting close to a return.
“(Rafaela) is doing much better, we’re getting close there, and Willson’s also doing much better, he was able to swing pretty aggressively in the cage again today,” Tracy said, adding that Rafaela was scheduled to run and Contreras was set to take batting practice on the field. “(We’ll) let them get through their whole day, see where they’re at and assess, but I think we’re getting pretty close with both of them.”
Staying ready
With the minor league season finished the Red Sox have sent a contingent of players who may potentially factor into the club’s plans the rest of the way to Fort Myers so they can stay ready in the event they’re needed.
Tracy did not have the full list of players available when asked Tuesday, but some of those headed to Fort Myers include pitchers Tanner Houck, Johan Oviedo, Jedixson Paez, Tyler Samaniego and Wyatt Olds, infielders Romy Gonzalez, Franklin Arias and Tsung-Che Cheng, and outfielder Braiden Ward.
Veteran catcher Tomas Nido has also come up from Worcester to serve as an extra catcher on the taxi squad for the Red Sox.
Extra innings
The Red Sox announced Eli White underwent successful Lisfranc repair surgery on his right foot Tuesday. The procedure was performed by Dr. Martin O’Malley at the Hospital for Special Surgery in New York City. … Aroldis Chapman (lat tightness) is feeling much better but is still a day or two away from a return to the mound. … Curtis Mead (fractured left wrist) has resumed swinging a regular bat and is taking overhand batting practice, but while the Red Sox haven’t ruled out a possible return, Tracy acknowledged that time isn’t on his side.

item.title: [NBC Sports Boston] Garrett Crochet says he's ready to 'get outs' for Red Sox
item.dc:creator: Michael Hurley
item.description: Once again, Garrett Crochet donned a full Red Sox uniform, made the walk from the bullpen to the mound, and pitched at Fenway Park on Tuesday afternoon. item.content:encoded:
Once again, Garrett Crochet donned a full Red Sox uniform, made the walk from the bullpen to the mound, and pitched at Fenway Park on Tuesday afternoon. This time, he faced a live hitter -- in the form of Ceddanne Rafaela -- as he took another step toward returning to the mound for Boston.
And for the first time in what's been a long recovery period, the 27-year-old said he feels ready to contribute.
"I would say, the way that that live [batting practice] just went, that I could go get outs," Crochet told reporters inside the Red Sox clubhouse.
That being said, Crochet shared that he has some hesitance to joining the roster, though it has nothing to do with his own health.
"This team's had a great year. I think that for me to take a spot on the roster, then someone would have to lose one. And I would feel bad doing that, because this team has pitched their ass off the whole season," Crochet said. "Ultimately, that's something that's gonna be up to the front office. And whenever they gauge that I'm ready, then I'll accept that. In the meantime, I'm just gonna keep working my butt off."
More Red Sox Coverage
Crochet's work on Tuesday involved 16 pitches, and he estimated he was sitting at 94-96 mph on his fastball velocity. The left-hander said how well he recovers on Wednesday will be a significant determinant on his ability to pitch in games. Yet when asked if he'll pitch in a regular-season game this weekend or save his return for the postseason, he is leaving that decision to chief baseball officer Craig Breslow and manager Chad Tracy.
"I think that I'm just gonna do whatever they tell me to do, to be honest," he said. "I think that [live BPs] and games, obviously it's a big step up and the pressure of the moment, I suppose, and the intensity. But I don't think that there's a set amount of [live BPs] that need to be thrown before a game."
Tracy, who officially dropped the interim tag earlier in the day, said that whatever decision is made on Crochet, it will be "done with Garrett's best interests in mind."
"Looking at what is he able to accomplish this week, and what does the playoffs require?" Tracy explained. "And then deciding can he fit that role or not based on what he's done."
Ceddanne Rafaela
Rafaela, who hasn't played since Sept. 2 due to a hamstring injury, partook in the live BP with Crochet as he nears a return to the lineup.
"Much better," Tracy said on Rafaela. "Getting close there."
Rafaela has produced the best offensive season of his career, as he's batted .282 with a .760 OPS in 135 games, while continuing to provide Gold Glove-level defense in center field.
Willson Contreras
Tracy also shared a positive injury update on Willson Contreras, who continues to improve after taking a pitch off his right hand last Thursday.
Tracy said that Contreras is "doing much better" and is "swinging aggressively" as he works his way back to full strength.
Aroldis Chapman
Closer Aroldis Chapman hasn't pitched since Sept. 13 due to some lat tightness, but Tracy had yet another positive injury update.
"He's getting very close," Tracy said. "I think we're a day or two away from him being ready to roll."
Group staying ready in Fort Myers
The Red Sox are keeping a team of reinforcements ready in Fort Myers for the playoff run, in case anybody is needed as an injury replacement along the way. That list of players includes:
- SP Tanner Houck
- SP Johan Oviedo
- SS/2B Franklin Arias
- OF Braiden Ward
- RP Wyatt Olds
- SS/2B Tsung-Che Cheng
- RP Tyler Samaniego
- 1B/2B Romy Gonzalez
- RP Jedixson Paez
Curtis Mead
Perhaps the lone negative injury update from Tracy was on second baseman Curtis Mead, who broke his wrist in his first game with the Red Sox on July 27.
"Haven't ruled it out yet. It's gonna be tough," Tracy said when asked if Mead might be able to return for the first round of the playoffs.
Tracy said that Mead is taking some overhand batting practice, but there may not be enough time for Mead to progress to being game-ready.
"I said we would probably be a little aggressive to see how the hand responds," Tracy said. "Have not ruled it out. It's just we're getting up against it a bit."

item.content:encoded:
Worcester: Cancelled (rain), end of season
Remember when Portland’s last game of the season was cancelled due to rain? Oh, that was just last week.
Well, as we’re stuck in a cycle of weekend storms, the last game of the season was cancelled for the WooSox. A factor in this decision was Worcester being eliminated from playoff contention on Saturday night. Still, for the season to end so unceremoniously calls for at least some commemoration, and so I’d like to shout out some names on the roster. I originally intended on going down the line on the website and speculate on future contributions to the team, but, by my estimation, especially since the trade for Adley Rutschman that had a ripple effect through the organization, a good portion of Worcester’s roster are either one-year placeholders until the farm gets replenished with the next couple of drafts or guys that are dealing with significant injuries. So, here’s to the guys that may not be that:
Allan Castro finished the season with 77 RBIs, two behind Bobby Dalbec for the team record since they relocated to Worcester five years ago… and saying that relocation happened six seasons ago is crazy for someone who went to the first home stand under pandemic crowd protocols. Castro really was a constant for the offense amidst a handful of platoon guys cycling through the team and that can’t be understated. He batted doubtful games back into contention and sealed close games away. If I pick a workhorse/general player of the year, it’s him or Braiden Ward, but only because Franklin Arias started the year in Portland.
Speaking of Braiden Ward, I personally was sad to see Brennan Bernardino go this offseason but loved the return from Colorado. And he performed fantastically, particularly near the end of the season. He ended up swiping 61 total bags and ther’s some clamor around a potential call-up to the Sox who, despite being a generally quick team in terms of baserunning, lack a real Dave Roberts-esque “when you see him, you know he’s going to steal” threat. Ward provides that, is defensively versatile, playing second as well as center field, and is pretty reliable with the bat in a pinch.
Franklin Arias is banging on the door and he will definitively be getting the call either in 2027 or Opening Day 2028, depending entirely on the length of the lockout. Either way, though, keeping him off the 40-man roster for now means, even with a lockout, he’ll get valuable time to improve his exceptional swing even more, though not against Major League arms. His totals across Portland and Worcester read like an All-Star caliber player: 28 home runs, .323/.400/.557 slash line, a 14% strikeout rate, and a plus glove in the infield to boot. Arias may or may not live up to his sky high prospect status, but pencil him in to the next iteration of this Red Sox team, whenever that comes.
John Holobetz will also likely be given the call in 2027. He’s still just 24. The 6’3” righty struck out 132 in 119 innings, walked just 36, had a WIP of a hair under 1.25, but even more comforting is he outperformed his Portland numbers in Worcester, signaling quick growth. While it’s sad that Quinn Priester missed 2026 with an injury, he was a world-beater in 2025, and the value of having steady presence in the rotation can’t be understated Depending how he bounces back in 2027, especially with the Brewers emerging as an NL front runner, expect that trade to go down in the history books as a win-win.
Hayden Mullins also put in his best work in 2026, and more specifically, directly before his promotion to Triple-A right before the end of the season. He celebrated his 26th birthday last Monday and so, in his age-25 season, Mullins was exactly what Portland needed in a rotation guy, especially following Anthony Eyannson’s departure. He struck out 132 in 92 innings, walked 49, lacked the longevity that Holobetz and others in the rotation had but did not give up long balls, getting taken yard just seven times all season (and even one of those was in his only Worcester appearance.) The 6’0” lefty will continue his development in 2027 before likely a late season call-up; it’s possible the team explores some multi-inning reliever roles depending on how this development goes.
Of course, too, the team’s former first-round draft pick Mikey Romero and current millionaire Kristian Campbell are still kicking around Wrocester, and the latter wants a redemption arc after a rough 2025. Neither saw any Major League time due to a cluttered roster and a multitude of other reasons, but don’t count either out for a platoon role next year, pending a lengthy lockout. You want guys looking better in September than they did in April, and while Campbell swung somewhat of a hot bat in the spring, I think that notion is true for both of these guys. The same is even true with Jedixson Paez (who saw Major League action, but don’t mention this to him) Blake Wehunt and Gage Ziehl. These are all guys to watch in 2027, provided some trade for a hole on the roster doesn’t call for dealing one of them (I think Campbell is pretty set on this roster given his price tag.) But, depth is a good problem to have.
And so ends my fourth full season providing Minor Lines for Over The Monster. You’ll see me kicking around during the playoff push and the offseason providing input on pieces that can make this 2027 team - and farm - even better than the 2026 version. Thanks so much for reading all season, and Go Sox!

item.content:encoded:
The WooSox roster has a bunch of guys who’ve made some plays for the Major League roster this season. But, as far as the Triple-A club is concerned, few guys (I know, I know, Franklin Arias might be one) have had as many big moments as Allan Castro. This wasn’t the 23-year-old’s strongest season from an OPS standpoint, but the big moments are getting notable. He just had a go-ahead home run the other day and he’s had multiple other walkoffs throughout the season. Yesterday, the WooSox again started a series on the winning side due to his bat, as he hit a 2-out single to score the Manfred runner. And, yes, in the process of all of this, Franklin Arias got himself a knock as did Romy Gonzalez. (Here’s that Castro hit.)
The game in general was a defensive battle. The Durham Bulls (Rays AAA) had the benefit of up-and-down starter Mason Englart dealing on Tuesday night as they couldn’t get on the board until Englart departed after seven. Luckily, Jedixson Paez was just as hot even without some of the strikeout numbers. His only run allowed was via a home run way back on the second at-bat of the game, and the 22-year-old righty recovered wonderfully from that, retiring fifteen consecutive Durham batters. From there, Tanner Houck came in and struck out the side in his rehab appearance, and it is starting to look likely that he sees some innings in a relief capacity as the Red Sox’s magic number dwindles. Osvaldo Berrios and Hobie Harris would then slam the door even in the face of a few more Bulls scoring opportunities; the WooSox had the only opportunity with runners in scoring position of the game. Enter extra innings, and enter Castro’s sealing single. Game over, 2-1.

item.content:encoded:
ARLINGTON, Texas — Among a series of minor injury updates offered by Red Sox interim manager Chad Tracy on Tuesday came some finality on one key reliever. Righty Justin Slaten, after further assessment by a renowned orthopedist in the Dallas area, won’t return to the Red Sox this year.
Slaten visited Dr. Keith Meister on Monday’s off day and testing on his injured elbow revealed “degenerative changes in the flexor mass,” according to Tracy. Slaten is set for a platelet-rich plasma (PRP) injection that is all but certain to rule out his return in 2026.
“It’s a big loss,” Tracy said, “at least now, with the finality of knowing we can’t have him back.”
Slaten was placed on the injured list with elbow inflammation in mid-August and dealt with recurring discomfort as he tried to resume throwing. As of the weekend, he was completely shut down from his progression. Now, he will receive the injection and rest in hopes of getting the issue fixed for 2027.
“Probably just means a chronic thing over time, but I’m speculating there,” Tracy said. “I just know that the conservative course of action is PRP, then he’s gonna rehab and go from there. Because of that, it’s probably going to cost him the rest of the season.”
Slaten appeared in 36 games for the Red Sox this year, posting a 4.60 ERA as a mid-relief option ahead of setup man Garrett Whitlock and closer Aroldis Chapman. For the third straight season, injuries were a big part of Slaten’s season. In 2024, he missed about six weeks due to elbow inflammation in July and August. Last season, he was out from June 1 to August 28 with a balky shoulder. This year, he suffered an oblique strain in early April and missed 31 games, then hit the IL again for the final six weeks.
Mead takes step forward
For the first time since having his left wrist broken by a wayward pitch in West Sacramento on July 27, Curtis Mead will do some offensive work in Boston on Wednesday. According to Tracy, Mead — who is out of a cast and has been doing defensive and baserunning drills for weeks — will hit lightly off a tee as he begins his swing progression.
“Mead will begin, tomorrow, introducing tee work,” Tracy said. “Obviously, we’ve talked a lot about the defensive stuff, being able to catch throws and he’s been doing that. Tomorrow, he’ll start doing some tee work with a light bat and then just kinda progress from there.”
With just 12 games left in the regular season, Mead is in a race against the clock to be fully ready for game action, a reality he acknowledged just last week. But it’s still notable that he’s ready to start taking swings in anticipation for potentially returning during the postseason if the Red Sox make a run.
Crochet throws again at Fenway
Left-hander Garrett Crochet took another small step toward a late-season return Tuesday, throwing a two-inning “up-and-down” bullpen (that includes a break simulating a between-inning breather) at Fenway Park. That session came four days after a one-inning high-intensity bullpen on the same mound.
“That went well,” said Tracy. “Everything went well.”
The next step for Crochet might be facing hitters in a live batting practice/simulated game setting but it’s very unlikely he’ll be ready to pitch in a rehab game before Triple-A Worcester’s season ends Sunday. A more likely scenario involves him getting into a simulated game or two and then making a relief appearance late in next week’s final homestand of the year.
“We’ll wait and see on the next steps,” Tracy said. “That was the most volume he’s had, so we’ll see how he feels and go from there.”
Guerrero close to return, Kelly has setback
Right-hander Tyron Guerrero, out since September 1 with shoulder inflammation, is with the Red Sox in Arlington and is expected to be activated before Wednesday’s game. Lefty Raymond Burgos and righty Wyatt Olds are the two leading candidates to be sent down as Guerrero takes a roster spot.
“We’ll see how everything goes with that today,” Tracy said.
The return of Guerrero will give the Red Sox another high-octane option at the end of a bullpen that also includes lefty Erik Miller, Whitlock and Chapman (and won’t have Slaten for the rest of the year).
One reliever who won’t contribute the rest of the way is righty Zack Kelly, who has been out since early July with a stress reaction in the olecranon (bone at the tip of the elbow). Kelly had been throwing live BP sessions in Fort Myers and was close to a rehab outing but had a setback last week and will undergo updated imaging this week.
Rafaela progressing
Center fielder Ceddanne Rafaela (right quad strain) has said his goal is to rejoin the Red Sox for this weekend’s series against the Rays and that is still in play. He’s back in Boston and going through strength tests on his leg while ramping up his running program.
“Started to increase running volume today,” Tracy said. “Nothing new to report there. He’ll continue to do that over the next 2-3 days and we’ll see where he’s at.”
The Red Sox could be careful with Rafaela and welcome him back early next week when the Guardians are at Fenway Park.
Houck, Oviedo on track for rehab outings
Right-hander Tanner Houck is pitching for the WooSox at Polar Park on Tuesday as planned. His outing was planned as a shorter relief outing (he entered in the seventh, following six strong innings for starter Jedixson Paez) and he’s expected to make another appearance over the weekend in a longer stint on the mound.
Right-hander Johan Oviedo is still on track to make a rehab start in Worcester on Thursday.
